A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CREMA research work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–D are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v2 reports original CREMA fine-tuning and zero-shot results across seven video-language benchmarks, together with ablations, efficiency measurements, and qualitative analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains those original empirical results and adds a VideoChat2/Mistral-7B experiment, design ablations, and attention visualizations.

M1.justification: Section 4.2 adds an implemented VideoChat2/Mistral-7B variant alongside the original BLIP-2/Flan-T5XL model. The MMQA adapters, self-gated fusion, sequential updates, and adaptive early-exit procedure remain unchanged. Appendix A.5's zero-shot fusion bypass is newly disclosed implementation information.

E1.justification: Both versions use SQA3D, MUSIC-AVQA, NExT-QA, TouchQA, ThermalQA, PerceptionTest, and VGGSound, with the same auxiliary pre-training sources. The new backbone experiment and design analyses reuse existing datasets, tasks, and modality coverage.

E2.justification: New Table 6 substantially expands the NExT-QA comparison with Video-LLaMA, Video-LLaVA, VideoChat2, MotionEpic-VoT, and LLaVA-NeXT, including a reproduced Mistral-7B VideoChat2 baseline. Earlier comparator sets remain; X-BLIP's appearance as X-InstructBLIP is only a naming change.

E3.justification: The new backbone evaluation introduces Mistral-7B with 16 frames alongside the retained Flan-T5XL 3B, four-frame experiments. Appendix B.8 also introduces controlled modality-prioritization and connector comparisons and 16/32/64-query-token settings. Existing splits, metrics, and original hyperparameter tables remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds backbone-portability validation and Appendix B.8 tests video versus depth prioritization, an FC connector versus interpolation, and query-length sensitivity. Figure 5 adds attention maps to an existing qualitative example. These extend the design evidence beyond the retained fusion, early-exit, sequential-training, pre-training, and LoRA-rank analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for its experimental results. The additional tables retain the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Existing result entries are retained. New Table 6 reports 78.9% and 79.4% for Mistral-based CREMA versus 78.4% for reproduced VideoChat2. These use different conditions from the retained 73.9% Flan-T5XL result. Tables 20–22 add depth-priority accuracy of 62.1%, interpolation accuracy of 78.9%, and query-length results, while reusing some earlier results as reference rows.

T1.justification: Equations 1–3, the low-rank parameterization, fusion definition, and gradient-based early-exit criterion are unchanged. The expanded training explanation introduces no new mathematical assumptions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract narrows the extensibility wording from incorporating 'any new modality' to 'many new modalities'. The principal claims about efficient modular fusion, seven-task performance, and reduced trainable parameters remain, as does the conclusion's broader extensibility claim.

C2.justification: Appendix B.8 adds interpretations concerning video prioritization, learnable feature alignment, and the accuracy–cost trade-off supporting 32 query tokens. A new Ethics Statement claims modality augmentation mitigates hallucinations without a dedicated evaluation. Appendix C's temporal-modeling and modality-extraction-overhead limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix A.4 newly states that comparisons share modality encoders and estimators. Appendix A.5 explains that existing two-modality zero-shot evaluations bypass fusion and concatenate tokens directly. These clarify retained experiments; the original hardware, hyperparameters, prompts, and code-access statements remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds brief positioning against MultiPLY and X-VILA and references for VideoChat2, BLIP-3, and Qwen2-VL. References to Brown et al., Kiela et al., and Tian et al. disappear. The central positioning against separate Q-Formers and universal multimodal encoders remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The introduction and sequential-training explanation receive localized revisions, with added backbone discussion, an Ethics Statement, and Appendix B.8. Citations switch to author–year format. Most prose and the main section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 redraws Figure 1 with explicit token/fusion graphics, adds comparison Table 6, ablation Tables 20–22, and attention-map Figure 5. Existing qualitative figures are redistributed across pages, and the document adopts different headers, heading styles, table sizing, and spacing. Earlier result displays remain identifiable.

improvement.justification: Table 6 provides empirical support for backbone portability, Tables 20–22 test previously unexamined design choices, and Appendix A.5 clarifies zero-shot inference. These strengthen an otherwise largely retained paper. The gain is limited by sparse training details for the new backbone experiment and the Ethics Statement's unevaluated hallucination-mitigation claim.
